transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I decided to come in because I just feel like I’m always up and moving around. Even on what's supposed to be a quiet day at home, I just... I keep bouncing from one thing to another. 

Like, I'll start looking at the garden club list, and then I'm over at my knitting bag, and then suddenly I'm going through travel papers. And I do all of that before I’ve really finished any one thing I actually started. I just can't seem to settle down, and I wanted to see what could be done about it.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts, even if it felt good at the time?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, I always feel restless, like I said, but it's not like a sudden burst of unusual energy where I don't need to sleep. I still sleep my normal hours, and my thoughts aren't racing out of control or anything. It's just this constant feeling of needing to be doing something, but never really finishing it.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks or notice that your attention shifts easily from one thing to another, even when you're trying to concentrate?

Yes, I do. It happens quite a bit, actually. I can start out listening at a planning meeting, or even just sitting down to read the church bulletin. I really try to pay attention, but... well, after a little while, I realize I’ve missed half of what was said or printed. My attention just drifts away, even when I'm trying my best to concentrate on it.
Do you often act on the spur of the moment without thinking things through, like making sudden decisions or saying things you later regret?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I might bounce around a lot during the day, but I don't really... jump into things without thinking. I'm actually pretty careful about what I say, and I don't go making big sudden decisions out of nowhere. So, no, I wouldn't say I do that.
Do these difficulties with restlessness and focusing interfere with your ability to function in your daily life, such as at work, in relationships, or with responsibilities at home?

Yes, it really does. It's... well, it has started causing some real strain, honestly. Mostly at home and down at the community center where I volunteer. It's just that my husband, and the other volunteers there, they can't really count on me to keep our plans straight anymore. Not unless someone is checking behind me to make sure I didn't mix things up or forget what I was supposed to be doing. So, yes, it definitely gets in the way.
Looking back, were you already experiencing these kinds of difficulties with restlessness and staying focused when you were a child, maybe even back in school?

Yes, I was. Even back in grade school, I remember my teachers telling my mother that I was bright, but... well, just scattered. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn, and just wiggling around in my seat before I ever finished my work. So, yes, it's been going on since I was a little girl.
Do you often feel irritable, easily frustrated, or experience mood swings that interfere with how you interact with others?

No, not really. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I forget things or mess up a schedule, but... no, I don't get irritable with other people. I don't have mood swings or anything like that. I'm usually pretty even-tempered, honestly.
